subject.title: fix(openrouter): apply request policy to music generation requests

question: Should OpenRouter music generation honor the existing provider-level allowPrivateNetwork opt-in, or should this capability retain its path-specific hard denial while honoring other request settings?
rationale: The implementation correctly exposes the existing configured policy through guarded transport, but deciding which provider capabilities may opt into private-network destinations is a security-boundary ownership choice rather than a correctness question automation should settle.

options.title: Honor configured opt-in
options.body: Allow the existing explicit operator setting to govern music generation through the shared guarded provider HTTP path, as this PR implements.

options.title: Retain the hard denial
options.body: Continue denying private-network destinations for music generation and forward only headers, proxy, authentication, and TLS-related request settings.

recommendation.title: Honor configured opt-in
recommendation.body: Allow the existing explicit operator setting to govern music generation through the shared guarded provider HTTP path, as this PR implements.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on the adjacent OpenRouter media provider and shared request-policy path provides the strongest available ownership signal.
